fieldMarks: Medium-sized rabbit, 14-19 in, 2-3.25 lb, with long ears, large hind legs and a short fluffy tail white underneath.
Upperparts reddish to grayish brown sprinkled with black; bright rust-coloured nape.
Grayish-white underparts with a brownish chest; tops of hind feet tan to whitish.
Tracks fall in groups of four, hind feet side by side; droppings are dark brown pea-sized pellets, often in piles.
behavior: Rests by day in a 'form' concealed in dense grass, a brush pile or thicket, seldom far from cover.
Feeds almost entirely on plants: grasses, wheat and clovers; in deep snow eats buds, twigs, bark and sprouts.
Breeds mid-February through September; nests are shallow ground cavities lined with grass and fur.
habitat: Edges between woody cover and open land: brushy or forest-border cover, meadows, orchards, farmland, hedgerows and second-growth shrubs.
range: From southern Manitoba and southern Quebec south through the eastern United States to the Great Plains, and on to Central and northwestern South America.

lookalikes.name: Swamp rabbit
lookalikes.howToTell: Swamp rabbit is larger with shorter, rounder ears, coarser yellowish fur, reddish-brown hind-foot tops and only a slightly rusty nape.

lookalikes.name: Black-tailed jackrabbit
lookalikes.howToTell: Jackrabbits are lanky with ears, hind legs and feet very large for the body.
